sentences.en: I mean, maybe he believes some of it, but I, I mean, this, the fact that he kept saying deep state and witch hunt, and I'm so confused.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许他相信了一部分，但我，我的意思是，这个，他一直把深层政府和政治迫害挂在嘴边，这让我感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: I've got to make some calls.
sentences.zh: 我得打几个电话。

sentences.en: I've got to try to figure out what this guy's deal is, because that raised more questions than it answered.
sentences.zh: 我得弄清楚这家伙到底在搞什么鬼，因为这引发的问题比解答的还要多。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，还不需要输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可免费获得30天访问权限。

sentences.en: And are Kevin and I chatting just between us, or are we doing this with a moderator?
sentences.zh: 我和凯文是私下闲聊，还是有主持人跟我们一起？

sentences.en: Kevin is actually hosting today.
sentences.zh: 凯文今天实际上是主持人。

sentences.en: Oh, cool, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 噢，酷，凯文。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Lucky me.
sentences.zh: 我真走运。

sentences.en: Do you realize that this is like, you're going to be like the most popular guy in the, in the entire valley?
sentences.zh: 你有没有意识到，这就像，你要成为整个湾区最受欢迎的家伙了？

sentences.en: Or like a poor man's Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 或者就像廉价版的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: That could, that could be it too.
sentences.zh: 那也，那也有可能。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: This is like when they're out of Oreos at the store, so you get the like off-brand, you know, Schmoreos.
sentences.zh: 这就像商店里的奥利奥卖光了，所以你买了个山寨货，你知道的，山寨奥利奥。

sentences.en: David Sanger is a national security correspondent.
sentences.zh: 大卫·桑格是一名国家安全记者。

sentences.en: He's the author of The Perfect Weapon, and he's our resident expert on cyber espionage.
sentences.zh: 他是《终极武器》的作者，也是我们常驻的网络间谍活动专家。

sentences.en: So going into the midterms, what do you think the Russians are up to?
sentences.zh: 那么谈到中期选举，你认为俄罗斯人在搞什么名堂？

sentences.en: So the way to think about the 2018 election for the Russians is that it's their spring training.
sentences.zh: 所以，看待俄罗斯人2018年选举的方式是，把这当作他们的春训。

sentences.en: They're out there trying some different moves,
sentences.zh: 他们在外面尝试一些不同的招数，

sentences.en: recognizing that the plays that worked two seasons ago probably aren't going to work now because everybody else in the big leagues has seen them.
sentences.zh: 意识到两个赛季前管用的战术现在可能不管用了，因为大联盟里的其他所有人都已经见识过了。

sentences.en: So they have to try some new plays, but they don't want to show too much because they need to leave some new techniques in reserve for 2020.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须尝试一些新战术，但又不想表现得太明显，因为他们需要为2020年保留一些新技术。

sentences.en: So if the 2018 elections are the sort of preseason training, the main season is 2020, the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果说2018年选举是某种季前训练，那么主赛季就是2020年，即总统大选。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So is Alexander Malkovich the kind of guy we should think of when we think about how Russia might be interfering in the midterm elections?
sentences.zh: 那么，当我们思考俄罗斯可能如何干预中期选举时，亚历山大·马尔科维奇是那种我们应该想到的家伙吗？

sentences.en: He's one of the kind of guys you should think of.
sentences.zh: 他是你应该想到的这类人之一。

sentences.en: He's not the kind of guy who's going in to steal emails from the Democratic National Committee or some other political entity.
sentences.zh: 他不是那种潜入民主党全国委员会或其他政治实体窃取电子邮件的家伙。

sentences.en: But instead, he's on the propaganda, information warfare side of the equation.
sentences.zh: 相反，他是站在宣传和信息战这一边的。

sentences.en: He's the kind of person who lives in this gray zone between fact and fiction, whose website picks up on real news stories in America, whether it's Megyn Kelly,
sentences.zh: 他是那种生活在事实与虚构之间的灰色地带的人，他的网站会关注美国的真实新闻故事，无论是梅根·凯利，

sentences.en: which they've leapt on, or Brett Kavanaugh, which they spent a lot of time on in recent weeks.
sentences.zh: 这是他们紧抓不放的，还是布雷特·卡瓦诺，他们在最近几周花了很多时间讨论他。

sentences.en: And he's taking what are some clear, familiar facts and then bending them in another direction.
sentences.zh: 他将一些清晰、熟悉的事实拿来，然后朝着另一个方向扭曲。

sentences.en: And that's the most subtle and effective form of propaganda.
sentences.zh: 这是最微妙、最有效的宣传形式。

sentences.en: And if it turns out that there are several million Americans who are really pulling down the USA really stuff the way there are millions of Americans who drive around listening to right-wing radio or left-wing blogs or whatever,
sentences.zh: 如果事实证明，有几百万美国人真的在把美国往下拉，就像有几百万美国人开车时听着右翼广播或左翼博客之类的东西一样，

sentences.en: then they're going to say this is a pretty cost-effective way to get through.
sentences.zh: 那么他们会觉得这是一种相当划算且能达成目标的途径。

sentences.en: So what other tests might they be running or what other things might the Russians be experimenting with this year?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们今年可能还在进行什么其他测试，或者俄罗斯人可能在试验什么其他事情？

sentences.en: The first thing they're doing is they're looking for generic, divisive issues.
sentences.zh: 他们做的第一件事是寻找普遍存在的分裂性议题。

sentences.en: So in 2016, that was the Black Lives Matter debate.
sentences.zh: 所以在2016年，那就是“黑人的命也是命”的辩论。

sentences.en: Or whether Hillary Clinton, by using her email at home, was actually a national security threat to the United States.
sentences.zh: 或者希拉里·克林顿在家使用电子邮件，是否实际上对美国构成了国家安全威胁。

sentences.en: Although none of the emails were marked classified at the time they were sent, it's more evidence that classified information may have been mishandled.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些邮件在发送时都没有被标记为机密，但这更是机密信息可能被错误处理的证据。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton's corruption is on a scale we have never seen before.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿的腐败达到了我们从未见过的规模。

sentences.en: So they're just amplifying existing schisms in the American debate.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是在放大美国辩论中现有的裂痕。

sentences.en: Skip forward to the 2018 election.
sentences.zh: 快进到2018年选举。

sentences.en: And the problem the Russians have right now is midterm elections are really hard to figure out.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人现在面临的问题是，中期选举非常难以捉摸。

sentences.en: There are roughly 470 candidates, right?
sentences.zh: 大约有470名候选人，对吧？

sentences.en: And the Russians don't want to sit around and debate, is Heidi Heitkamp good for me or bad for me?
sentences.zh: 而俄罗斯人不想坐下来争论，海蒂·海特坎普对我来说是好是坏？

sentences.en: If flood insurance is $500 a month, that pretty much locks people out of home ownership.
sentences.zh: 如果洪水保险是每月500美元，那就基本把人们挡在了购房门槛之外。

sentences.en: We can't have that happen.
sentences.zh: 我们不能让这种事发生。

sentences.en: So we need to have flood protection in Minot, and we need to get going on it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要在迈诺特提供防洪保护，我们需要开始行动了。

sentences.en: So they are once again looking for divisive issues, and we're busy providing them.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们再次寻找分裂性的议题，而我们正忙着为他们提供。

sentences.en: The Democrat Party is openly inviting millions of illegal aliens to break our laws, violate our borders, and overwhelm our nation.
sentences.zh: 民主党公开邀请数百万非法外国人打破我们的法律、践踏我们的边境并压垮我们的国家。

sentences.en: This will be, this is a circus.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场闹剧。

sentences.en: An election.
sentences.zh: 一场选举。

sentences.en: Boy, y'all want power.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你们可真想要权力啊。

sentences.en: God, I hope you never get it.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑，我希望你们永远得不到它。

sentences.en: Of Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 关于卡瓦诺的。

sentences.en: I hope the American people can see through this champ.
sentences.zh: 我希望美国人民能看穿这场骗局。

sentences.en: The caravan.
sentences.zh: 大篷车队。

sentences.en: This invasion of our sovereignty, it's, we've got to stop it.
sentences.zh: 这是对我们主权的侵犯，我们必须阻止它。

sentences.en: Law and order.
sentences.zh: 法律与秩序。

sentences.en: A Florida man suspected of mailing bombs to high-profile Democrats.
sentences.zh: 一名佛罗里达男子涉嫌向知名民主党人邮寄炸弹。

sentences.en: And common sense.
sentences.zh: 还有常识。

sentences.en: That's what it's going to be.
sentences.zh: 事情就会是这样。

sentences.en: The Trump administration officials are considering legally defining gender as somebody's biological sex at birth.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府官员正在考虑从法律上将性别定义为某人出生时的生物学性别。

sentences.en: A move that could jeopardize the rights of more than a million transgender Americans.
sentences.zh: 此举可能会危及超过一百万跨性别美国人的权利。

sentences.en: It's going to be an election of those things.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场围绕这些事情的选举。

sentences.en: Secondly, the Russians are fabulous at getting inside email systeMs.
sentences.zh: 其次，俄罗斯人非常擅长侵入电子邮件系统。

sentences.en: But what they discovered in 2016 was that they didn't cover their tracks very well as they made the emails public.
sentences.zh: 但他们在2016年发现的是，他们在公开这些电子邮件时并没有很好地掩盖自己的行踪。

sentences.en: They know that people will be on the lookout in the future for the mass release of emails and probably call the Russians out.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，未来人们会对大规模泄露电子邮件保持警惕，并可能会揭发俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: So, what the Russians are looking for is,
sentences.zh: 所以，俄罗斯人正在寻找的是，

sentences.en: are there more subtle things that they could do with information that they gleaned from breaking into computer systems and computer networks?
sentences.zh: 他们能否用从入侵计算机系统和计算机网络中收集到的信息做一些更微妙的事情？

sentences.en: Maybe next time you don't release the entire email, but you tip off reporters to stories that are found from those emails and try to get something up and running.
sentences.zh: 也许下次你不是泄露整封电子邮件，而是向记者透露从这些电子邮件中发现的故事线索，并试图让某些事情发酵运转起来。

sentences.en: So, that would be a second category.
sentences.zh: 所以，这将是第二个类别。

sentences.en: The third category could well be physical attacks.
sentences.zh: 第三个类别很可能是物理攻击。

sentences.en: If you can figure out how to turn off the lights in a certain city or a certain congressional district,
sentences.zh: 如果你能想办法让某个城市或某个国会选区的灯熄灭，

sentences.en: you might have a significant capability in depressing the turnout in areas where you think there's going to be a close race.
sentences.zh: 你可能就具备了在认为会有势均力敌竞选的地区压低投票率的强大能力。

sentences.en: And that just seems crazy.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Could they actually do that?
sentences.zh: 他们真的能做到吗？

sentences.en: Could they turn off the lights in a polling station in a contested district somewhere in America?
sentences.zh: 他们能在美国某个竞争激烈的选区的投票站里关掉电灯吗？

sentences.en: They've certainly positioned themselves to.
sentences.zh: 他们当然已经为此做好了准备。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: it was only last spring that the Department of Homeland Security came out with this very detailed report about how the Russians had placed malware in the major nuclear plants and other parts of the electric utility grid.
sentences.zh: 就在去年春天，国土安全部发布了一份非常详细的报告，指出俄罗斯人如何在主要核电站和电力公用事业网的其他部分植入了恶意软件。

sentences.en: And, of course, what they couldn't tell you is what the Russians planned to do with that.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们无法告诉你的是俄罗斯人计划用这些来做什么。

sentences.en: Maybe they're just there monitoring our energy efficiency.
sentences.zh: 也许他们只是在那里监测我们的能源效率。

sentences.en: But the fear, of course, is that they want to be in a position to flip the lights off.
sentences.zh: 但当然，人们的恐惧是他们想要处于能够随时拉闸断电的位置。

sentences.en: And there's a record for this.
sentences.zh: 而且这有据可查。

sentences.en: All you have to do is go to Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 你只需要去乌克兰看看。

sentences.en: There were two significant attacks that the Russians organized against power grids in different parts of Ukraine simply to make the point that they could turn off the power whenever they wanted.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人对乌克兰不同地区的电网发动了两次重大袭击，仅仅是为了表明他们随时可以切断电源。

sentences.en: And the stories that come out of that are pretty chilling.
sentences.zh: 由此产生的故事相当令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: I went out and interviewed operators of power plants in Ukraine who had been sitting at their computers and suddenly discovering that the mouse was operating by itself,
sentences.zh: 我曾去乌克兰采访过那些电网的操作员，他们当时正坐在电脑前，突然发现鼠标在自己动，

sentences.en: that an arrow was moving around on their screens and flipping off substations all around their district of Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 屏幕上的箭头在移动，并切断了乌克兰他们辖区周围的所有变电站，

sentences.en: turning off the power until finally at the end it turned off the power inside the control room.
sentences.zh: 切断了电源，直到最后连控制室内部的电源也被切断了。

sentences.en: And it was all being done by remote control, probably from Russia.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是通过远程控制完成的，很可能来自俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And I want you to sort of try to help me close this gap that I'm feeling where it feels like there's kind of a tension here where, on one hand, we now have all these reasons,
sentences.zh: 我想请你帮我缩小我所感受到的这种差距，这里似乎有一种紧张关系：一方面，鉴于我们在2016年所看到的以及2018年迄今所听到的，我们现在有了所有这些理由，

sentences.en: given what we saw in 2016 and what we've heard about so far in 2018, for people to be very skeptical of the integrity of the election process.
sentences.zh: 让人们对选举过程的完整性持高度怀疑态度。

sentences.en: You know, you know, you have no idea which posts on your feed are written by foreign nationals in which influence operation, you know, we can't necessarily trust our voter data.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你根本不知道你信息流里的哪些帖子是由外国国民在哪个影响力行动中撰写的，你知道，我们不一定能信任我们的选民数据。

sentences.en: We can't necessarily trust our polling places to be safe.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定能信任我们的投票点是安全的。

sentences.en: On the other hand, what some of this interference is trying to do is sort of sow that distrust, that it might actually be the point of what they're doing to create that distruSt.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，其中一些干预企图做的是播下这种不信任的种子，制造这种不信任感可能正是他们所做事情的目的所在。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, how should our listeners, how should we think about going to the polls on Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，我们的听众应该如何看待周二的投票？

sentences.en: What should people be feeling as they go to vote?
sentences.zh: 人们去投票时应该有什么样的感受？

sentences.en: Well, you've touched, Kevin, on the great information warfare paradox,
sentences.zh: 凯文，你触及了伟大信息战的悖论，

sentences.en: which is you don't have to do a successful cyber attack on a voting system or even on the communications we have about where candidates stand,
sentences.zh: 那就是你不需要对投票系统甚至我们关于候选人立场的沟通进行成功的网络攻击，

sentences.en: what kind of positions people are taking on the divisive issues of our day.
sentences.zh: 不需要对人们在我们时代的分裂性议题上采取什么样的立场进行攻击。

sentences.en: All you need to do is sow fear into the system.
sentences.zh: 你所需要做的就是在系统中播下恐惧的种子。

sentences.en: And the Russians were successful of doing that in 2016.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人在2016年成功做到了这一点。

sentences.en: And to some degree, they are reaping the benefits of that in 2018.
sentences.zh: 并在某种程度上，他们在2018年收获了这些成果。

sentences.en: So if you're sitting around repeating the rumors, oh, my vote's been manipulated, it won't count, and so forth, first of all,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你坐在那里重复那些谣言，哦，我的投票被操纵了，它不会被计算在内，等等，首先，

sentences.en: you're probably wrong because the hardest thing for the Russians to do is to get into the voting system itself.
sentences.zh: 你可能是错的，因为俄罗斯人最难做到的一件事就是侵入投票系统本身。

sentences.en: But secondly, you're playing into their hands.
sentences.zh: 但其次，你正中他们的下怀。

sentences.en: You know, so it's not just the sabotage of the system.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以这不仅仅是对系统的破坏。

sentences.en: It's the fear that the sabotage could be successful that is the Russians' greatest weapon.
sentences.zh: 对破坏可能成功的恐惧才是俄罗斯人最大的武器。

sentences.en: Thanks, David.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，大卫。

sentences.en: Thanks so much, guys.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，伙计们。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日秀》（The Daily）的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Kevin Roos.
sentences.zh: 我是凯文·罗斯。

sentences.en: Michael Barbaro will be back tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·巴巴罗明天将回归。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种一觉睡到天亮的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会晕厥过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用上或在你喜欢收听播客的任何地方寻找《Wirecutter秀》。
